orchestkit · issue #3220

58 tests that never run

run-all-tests.sh dispatches by explicit line, never by glob. A test file nobody wires up simply never executes. It cannot fail, so it cannot warn, and it rots quietly against code that moved on. An orphaned test is worse than a missing one, because the file's existence implies coverage that is not there.

of 241 never executed

passed when run by hand

real bugs in the 1 that failed

ratchet runtime

all 58 executed individually during triage · 0 flagged as risky beforehand

The one that failed had two real defects

tests/plugins/test-cc-discovery-simulation.sh, invisible for as long as it went unwired: 

1. a path that stopped existing
  - PLUGIN_JSON="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude-plugin/plugin.json"
  + PLUGIN_ROOT="$PROJECT_ROOT/plugins/ork"
  the plugin moved under plugins/ork/ with the single-plugin layout

2. a bug that could never have passed on any machine
  - ((total_skills++))          # under set -e
  + total_skills=$((total_skills + 1))
  post-increment returns the value BEFORE incrementing, so at 0 it
  returns 1 and set -e kills the script on the very first skill

Neither would have been found without running an orphan by hand. That is the argument for the ratchet in one example.

Why a ratchet at 58 and not a hard zero

Zero would mean wiring all 58 into the runner here. They pass, so that is low-risk, but it is a real CI-time increase that deserves its own measurement rather than riding along in a bug-fix change. The ratchet freezes the debt meanwhile: a NEW unreferenced test file fails CI the day it is written, which is precisely the failure mode that produced these 58. Baseline may only fall.

The measurement trap, twice

AttemptResultWhy
narrow grep scope107 orphansonly searched package.json, workflows and two shallow globs, so it missed references from deeper paths
whole tracked tree58 orphanscorrect
one git grep per fileover 2 minutes241 subprocesses, too slow for test:skills
single pass in memory8 secondsread each tracked file once, match all names against it

Narrow search scope produces false positives AND false negatives. This is the same family as the linter that reported DEAD-EDGE: 0 in #3216 while five edges sat in front of it, so the ratchet is proven by control: adding a throwaway orphan makes it exit 1, removing it returns exit 0.

Deliberately not claimed

15 other test files pair set -e with a post-increment. They are candidates, not confirmed bugs: most run green in CI every day, which proves their counters do not start at zero. Reporting them as 15 bugs would be the false-positive mirror of the false-negatives above. Worth a lint rule, not a claim.
